p01.why: The lambda calls a consteval function with its parameter, so the lambda becomes consteval, and call(3) in a constexpr initializer is a constant expression.

p02.why: Loops and changes to local variables are allowed in constant evaluation, and sum(4) is 10.

p03.why: A constexpr function from a template that calls a consteval function with a parameter becomes consteval, and forward_square(3) is constant.

p04.why: A namespace-scope constexpr reference can bind to a temporary, which becomes static and const, so reading it is allowed.

p05.why: A constexpr variable is const, so assigning to it is an error.

p06.why: constinit appears only after the initializing declaration; the specification records that Clang rejects this and GCC and EDG accept it (Q-0025).

p07.why: The two declarations of f disagree on constexpr.

p08.why: A class with a volatile non-static member is not a literal type, so it cannot be the type of a constexpr variable.

p09.why: The reference and the pointer refer to a variable with static storage duration.

p10.why: constinit is on the initializing declaration, and the initializer is constant.

p11.why: A declaration cannot have both constinit and constexpr.

p12.why: An earlier declaration may leave out constinit as long as the initializing declaration has it.

p13.why: The consteval call returns a pointer to storage it allocated and did not free, so the call is not a constant expression.

p14.why: f(true) returns before reaching the non-constant static variable, so the evaluation never reaches it.

p15.why: The initializer calls a function that is not constexpr, so it is not a constant expression.

p16.why: Taking the address of a consteval function is allowed in the body of another consteval function, and the call through the pointer is constant.

p17.why: square works both in the static_assert and at run time, and square(argc) equals argc*argc, so main returns 0.

p18.why: Both calls to square have constant arguments, so each call is a constant expression, also in the initializer of the non-constexpr b.

p19.why: The static_assert evaluation calls read, which is not constexpr.

p20.why: The constexpr pointer is static and points to another static variable, which has static storage duration.

p21.why: A declaration that only defines a class cannot be constexpr.

p22.why: A constexpr pointer cannot point to an automatic variable.

p23.why: f is an ordinary function, so the call square(x) with a non-constant argument is not a constant expression and f does not become consteval.

p24.why: Derived has a base whose destructor is user-provided and not constexpr, so Derived is not a literal type.

p25.why: At namespace scope the temporary bound to the reference member becomes static, the read of the const scalar temporary is allowed, and main returns 0; the Q-0193 note on EDG may make this depend.

p27.why: Each static or thread_local variable reached is usable in constant expressions, and returning the address of a static object is a valid constant pointer.

p28.why: Holder has a member whose class has a non-constexpr user destructor, so Holder is not a literal type.

p29.why: Every member has a default member initializer, so the implicit default constructor gives every member a value and the variable needs no initializer.

p30.why: The inner calls are inside a consteval function, an immediate function context, and quad(2) is constant.

p32.why: twice is inline, so both translation units can define it, and both calls give the expected values, so main returns 0.

p33.why: The constexpr variable has no initializer and the implicit default constructor leaves x without a value.

p34.why: constinit is only on the earlier declaration; Clang (pedantic) and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0025).

p35.why: A union is literal only if at least one member is not volatile, and here every member is volatile.

p36.why: A declaration cannot have both consteval and constexpr.

p37.why: height has no default member initializer, so the variable without an initializer leaves a member without a value.

p38.why: A constexpr reference in a block without static cannot refer to an automatic variable.

p39.why: The namespace-scope pointer selects the non-consteval f(long), and inside the consteval g, selecting the consteval f(int) is allowed.

p40.why: A constexpr function that never gives a constant is valid; the specification records that Clang 18 rejects it and newer versions accept it (Q-0020).

p41.why: The initializer calls a function that is not constexpr, so it is not a constant initializer.

p42.why: The goto is on a path that f(true) does not reach.

p43.why: wrap is a plain constexpr function, not one from a template, so its call to sq with a non-constant argument is rejected.

p44.why: A constexpr function with a non-literal return type that never gives a constant is valid; Clang 18 rejects it and newer compilers accept it (Q-0020).

p45.why: A constexpr int needs an initializer.

p46.why: The address of a consteval function is taken outside an immediate function context.

p47.why: constinit does not make the variable const, so main can change it to 6 and return 0.

p48.why: The evaluation reaches a static variable that is not usable in constant expressions.

p49.why: A non-literal parameter type is allowed; Clang 18 rejects it and newer versions accept it (Q-0020).

p50.why: Logged has a user destructor that is not constexpr, so it is not a literal type.

p51.why: Each call to twice has constant arguments, consteval functions are inline, and main returns 0.

p52.why: S has a destructor that is not constexpr, so it is not a literal type.

p53.why: constinit applies to variables with static or thread storage duration, and a function is not a variable.

p54.why: The lambda becomes consteval, so g, an ordinary function, calls it with a non-constant argument.

p55.why: A constexpr reference in a block without static must not bind to a temporary.

p56.why: The variable of non-literal type is on a path that f(true) does not reach.

p57.why: The consteval call divides by zero, which is undefined, so the call is not a constant expression.

p58.why: A pointer one past the end of a static array and a pointer to a function are both allowed in a constexpr variable.

p59.why: The constexpr default constructor with the default member initializer gives start the value 1.

p60.why: The constexpr constructor gives a constant initializer, and constinit does not need a constexpr destructor.

p61.why: A block constexpr aggregate's reference member cannot bind to a temporary.

p62.why: A constexpr int has type const int and can be used as an array bound.

p63.why: The declarations of f disagree on consteval.

p64.why: A block variable without static has automatic storage, so it cannot be constinit.

p65.why: constinit does not add const, so the type of counter is int.

p66.why: The target type selects the consteval f(int), which takes its address outside an immediate function context.

p67.why: The initializer calls a function that is not constexpr.

p68.why: Static and thread_local block variables have static and thread storage duration, so constinit is allowed.

p69.why: A static constexpr array is usable in constant expressions, so the evaluation may reach it.
